mechanism_narrative: A rebound in WORKPLACES mobility from -35.7 at t-2w to -19.7 at t-0w signals resumption of commuting and workday routines that historically co-move with retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved by 16 points between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is lower than its trailing 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 3 points week-on-week (as it did from -34.4 to -30.1), this indicates renewed use of public transport for shopping and leisure trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -34.4 to -30.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after a TRANSIT improvement exceeding 3 points, observed in a majority of comparable weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a joint unlocking of commuting and transit-dependent shopping trips; when both rise together for two consecutive weeks, their combined effect on RETAIL_REC exceeds the sum of either alone, driving a stronger four-week increase.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean does not exceed its trailing mean despite concurrent two-week improvements in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in PARKS from 36.3 at t-2w (Easter holiday peak) to -7.1 at t-0w marks the end of the holiday outdoor-leisure substitution effect; as outdoor leisure fades, demand shifts back toward retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week following a holiday peak
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 14.0 to -7.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop exceeding 15 points after a holiday peak, in most comparable historical holiday transitions.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -20 (indicating relaxed occupancy or capacity restrictions on offices and businesses), this signals a broader policy loosening that extends to retail capacity limits, boosting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses above -20 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -19.7 at t-0w, its highest value in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of WORKPLACES crossing above -20, indicating the threshold does not proxy for retail-relevant policy changes.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (near 0, ranging -3.3 to 3.4) combined with a slight decline in RESIDENTIAL (10.0 to 8.7) indicates households are maintaining essential-trip patterns while modestly reducing time at home; this joint pattern signals cautious, not expansive, behavioral change, limiting the upside for discretionary RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines less than 2 points while GROCERY_PHARM stays within +/-5 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined only 1.3 points over the snapshot while GROCERY_PHARM stayed near zero
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean exceeds its trailing mean despite RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM both remaining in their narrow stable ranges.

mechanism_narrative: During the early post-Easter weeks in Madrid, residual holiday-driven outdoor activity (evidenced by the PARKS spike at t-2w) tends to persist intermittently through April, periodically diverting potential retail visits to parks and outdoor spaces, dampening RETAIL_REC growth whenever PARKS remains elevated relative to its pre-holiday baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS values remained elevated (6.7 to 36.3) for three of four snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises even as PARKS remains above its pre-holiday baseline level of roughly 5-10 percent change, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility falls below -35 percent change from baseline, indicating a tightening of mobility restrictions or renewed caution around public transport, this precedes a reduction in retail footfall as fewer transit-dependent shoppers can reach retail destinations.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached a snapshot low of -34.4 at t-1w, close to the -35 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks following a TRANSIT reading below -35, indicating the threshold is not predictive of retail activity.
